# Draft:Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm for Training Feed-Forward Multilayer Perceptrons

----
Proposed use of the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm in multilayer perceptron training refers to a published metaheuristic-based approach in which the Secretary bird optimization algorithm (SBOA) is used to optimize the weights and biases of a multilayer perceptron (MLP). In the published formulation, the trainable parameters of the network are represented as candidate solutions in the SBOA search space, and the optimization objective is defined using mean squared error (MSE).
Background
Multilayer perceptrons are widely used artificial neural network models for classification and regression tasks. In addition to gradient-based methods such as backpropagation, the use of metaheuristic algorithms for neural-network training has also been widely discussed in the literature.
The Secretary bird optimization algorithm was introduced in 2024 as a population-based optimization method inspired by the hunting and escape behaviour attributed to secretary birds. A later review discussed variants and applications of SBOA across several optimization domains.
Method
In the published SBOA-based training scheme, the weights and biases of the MLP are encoded as a single optimization vector. For a single-hidden-layer feed-forward network, the hidden-layer net input is written as
h_j=\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_{ij}x_i+b_j
where x_i denotes the input, w_{ij} the weight between input node i and hidden node j, and b_j the hidden-layer bias.
Using the sigmoid activation function, the hidden-layer output is
H_j=\frac{1}{1+e^{-h_j}}
The output-layer net input is
o_k=\sum_{j=1}^{h} w_{jk}H_j+B_k
and the final output is
O_k=\frac{1}{1+e^{-o_k}}
where w_{jk} denotes the hidden-to-output weight and B_k denotes the output-layer bias.
The full trainable parameter set is represented as
\mathbf{V}=(w_{ij}\cup w_{jk}\cup b_j\cup B_k)
so that each candidate solution corresponds to one complete parameterization of the network.
Optimization
SBOA is a population-based optimization algorithm in which candidate solutions are initialized within predefined lower and upper bounds. In the original SBOA formulation, initialization is written as
X_{i,j}=lb_j+r\cdot(ub_j-lb_j)
where lb_j and ub_j are the lower and upper bounds for dimension j, and r is a random number in the interval [0,1].
In the SBOA–MLP training setting, each candidate vector is decoded into network weights and biases, and the resulting neural-network error is used as the fitness value.
Objective function
In the published formulation, training is posed as a minimization problem based on mean squared error:
\mathrm{MSE}=\frac{1}{U}\sum_{u=1}^{U}(y_u-\hat{y}_u)^2
where y_u is the target output, \hat{y}_u is the predicted output, and U is the number of training samples.
The optimization objective is therefore written as
\min F(\mathbf{V})=\mathrm{MSE}
where \mathbf{V} denotes the vector of trainable MLP parameters.
Context
The use of metaheuristic algorithms for training feed-forward neural networks predates SBOA-based formulations and has been explored with many other optimizers. Within that broader literature, the SBOA-based method has been presented as one published application of a recently introduced optimizer to MLP training.
